resources.string: Your phone, your private music server
Sharing with approved devices. Tap Stop to end sharing.
Music server stopped to protect battery (below 15%).
Could not start the server. Check app permissions and try again with the app open.
Keep your music on a spare phone. Listen here or on a device you approve, without uploading your library.
Get an invitation from the phone hosting your music. The host approves your device before playback.
Stop the server to change the shared selection.
Load music in the device library first.
Choose an address reachable from the other phone. For outside access, use a private VPN address or your own configured HTTPS address.
Valid for 10 minutes and one device. Share privately. You still approve the connection on this phone.
This invitation is invalid or expired. Ask the host for a new one.
Enter a server address, for example https://192.168.1.20:8898
Check that %1$s is also shown on the host phone, then approve this device there.
Approval timed out. Create a new invitation and try again.
This device will lose access to the library and ongoing audio transfers will end.
Connected servers will appear here. Your credentials stay on this device.
Remove this server from this phone? Saved playlists keep their references and need a new connection to play.
The server identity stays pinned when you change networks. The new address is checked before saving.
Use search or a genre to find more music without loading the whole library.
No matching songs. Try another search or genre.
Allow local network access to connect these phones. Music permission is also needed when hosting.

1. Run the server on the phone with your music.
2. Put both phones on the same private VPN (for example WireGuard or Tailscale), or configure a reachable address yourself.
3. Create an invitation using the host’s VPN address. Already paired? Change the saved server address.
4. Keep the host powered and the VPN connected.

T2Rhythm provides no central relay and does not open router ports automatically. Cellular networks may block direct incoming connections.
Sharing keeps this phone awake. Keep a spare phone plugged in. Below 15% battery, an unplugged server stops automatically. Device battery-saving rules may also interrupt hosting.
TLS encryption · explicit device approval · revocable access. Shared audio is not saved in the client’s audio cache.
